AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance to AI coding agents when working with code in this repository. It is harness-agnostic: any agent that reads repo-level instructions should use it.

Overview

PKPDsim is an R package for simulating pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) mixed-effects models. It uses ODE-based numerical integration (via Rcpp + Boost odeint) and ADVAN-style analytical solutions.

The package is on CRAN, so changes must keep R CMD check --as-cran clean.

Commands

# Load package for interactive development
devtools::load_all()

# Run all tests
devtools::test()

# Run a single test file
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test_advan.R")

# Run a subset of test files (preferred: this also runs tests/testthat/setup.R,
# which many test files depend on for their shared, pre-compiled models)
devtools::test(filter = "advan")

# Regenerate NAMESPACE and man/ from roxygen2 comments
devtools::document()

# Full R CMD check
devtools::check()

# Build documentation site
pkgdown::build_site()

Notes:

  • Run devtools::document() after touching any roxygen2 block; NAMESPACE and man/*.Rd are generated, never edit them by hand.
  • Tests and examples that compile models are slow. Several are gated behind NOT_CRAN=true (see tests/testthat/setup.R); set that env var locally to exercise the full suite.
  • C++ in src/ is compiled at package install time. After editing src/*.cpp, re-run devtools::load_all() (which recompiles) rather than relying on a cached build. If a src/RcppExports.cpp signature changes, run Rcpp::compileAttributes().

Architecture

Core simulation pipeline

new_ode_model() / (pre-built ADVAN models)
    ↓
sim()  →  compiled C++ ODE solver (Boost odeint RK4)
    ↓
data.frame output (compartment amounts × time)

sim() and sim_core() are siblings, not a chain: sim() never calls sim_core(). Both end up calling the compiled ode object directly.

sim() branches: if analytical is supplied it skips ODE solving entirely and routes through advan() / advan_create_data() / advan_parse_output() (R/sim.R, around the “Use analytical equations (ADVAN)” block). Otherwise it builds an event table and calls the dynamically compiled ODE solver.

Key function files

  • R/new_ode_model.R — Defines ODE models: takes user-supplied C++ ODE code as a string, transforms it (index-shifting, auto-declaring variables, injecting infusion rate terms), then compiles it dynamically via Rcpp::sourceCpp(). This is the entry point for custom models.
  • R/sim.R — Main user-facing simulation function. Handles input validation, covariate interpolation, IIV sampling and application, event-table construction, and then either calls the compiled ode object or routes to the ADVAN analytical path.
  • R/sim_core.R — Separate fast entry point for iterative use (estimation, optimal design). It consumes a precalculated design — e.g. the object from sim(..., return_design = TRUE) — and calls the compiled ode with no validation.
  • R/advan.R — Large (~41KB) file implementing ADVAN1–5 analytical solutions for standard PK models without ODE solving.
  • R/compile_sim_cpp.R — Transforms user ODE strings into compilable C++ and calls Rcpp::sourceCpp().
  • R/shift_state_indices.R — Rewrites compartment indices in ODE code (R is 1-based, C++ is 0-based) before compilation.
  • R/translate_ode.R — Translates ODE code between PKPDsim and RxODE syntax.
  • R/calculate_parameters.R — Convenience wrapper around sim_ode() that returns model-specific / effective parameters and variables (e.g. CLi from CL and covariates). Not used by sim() itself.
  • R/create_event_table.R — Builds the design matrix (event table) used by the C++ solver.
  • R/model_library.R — Named library of standard structural models (pk_1cmt_iv, pk_2cmt_iv_auc, pk_1cmt_iv_mm, pk_*_oral, …), each a list of ODE code plus obs/dose defaults. This is what new_ode_model("pk_1cmt_iv") resolves against.
  • R/new_regimen.R, R/new_covariate.R — Constructors for the two other main user-facing inputs to sim(); regimen joining/shifting helpers live in R/join_regimen.R, R/shift_regimen.R, R/merge_regimen.R.

C++ layer

  • inst/cpp/sim.cpp, inst/cpp/sim_header.cpp — Template for the dynamically compiled ODE solver using Boost odeint. User ODE code is injected here at compile time.
  • src/*.cpp — Pre-compiled Rcpp functions for standard analytical PK models (1-, 2-, 3-compartment IV/oral).
  • src/Makevars — Sets PKG_CPPFLAGS = -D_HAS_AUTO_PTR_ETC=0 (needed for Boost with newer C++ standards).

Two distinct compilation paths exist and should not be confused: src/ is compiled once when the package is installed, while user ODE models are compiled at runtime into a temporary shared object (or an installed model package).

Model definition formats

  • Custom models: C++ ODE string passed to new_ode_model(code = "...")
  • Library models: named entries in R/model_library.R, e.g. new_ode_model("pk_1cmt_iv")
  • Literature models: JSON5 files in inst/models/, loaded via read_model_json() and installable as standalone packages via install_default_literature_model()
  • API models: fetched at runtime via model_from_api()

When new_ode_model(package = "...") is used, the model is emitted as a real R package scaffolded from inst/template/ (its R/ files carry parameters, IIV, IOV, RUV, fixed parameters and the compiled model object). Changes to model metadata usually need a matching change in that template.

ODE code conventions

User-facing ODE code may index compartments from either A[0] or A[1]. shift_state_indices() subtracts 1 from every index, but returns the code untouched if that would produce a negative index — so already-0-based code is left alone. new_ode_model(as_is = TRUE) disables this rewriting (and line-ending substitution) entirely. Variables that are not parameters or covariates must be listed in declare_variables, otherwise the generated C++ will not compile. pk_code runs once at initialization and then at each event, before that interval is integrated — not before every derivative evaluation, since RK4 evaluates the ODE several times within an interval, so do not put per-derivative logic there. state_init initializes compartment amounts.

Variability modeling

IIV is sampled and applied in R/sim.R: mvrnorm2() draws the ETAs, and the omega_type block applies them per parameter. Accepted omega_type values are exponential (TVPAR * exp(ETA)) and normal (TVPAR + ETA).

IOV is different: R/new_ode_model.R generates the kappa_* bin logic into the model C++ at compile time, and the compiled solver picks the right bin at runtime from the iov_bins passed through sim().

Mixture models and quasi-random (Halton/Sobol) sampling are supported via randtoolbox.

Interoperability

R/pkpdsim_to_nlmixr.R, R/nlmixr_parse_parameters.R, R/regimen_to_nm.R and R/nm_to_regimen.R convert models and regimens to/from nlmixr2 and NONMEM.

Testing patterns

Tests live in tests/testthat/ (testthat edition 3).

  • tests/testthat/setup.R compiles a set of shared models once per test session (mod_1cmt_iv, pk_iov, mod_mixture, …). Reuse those objects instead of calling new_ode_model() inside a test — compilation dominates runtime. Add new shared fixtures there when several files need them.
  • Expensive fixtures in setup.R are wrapped in if (identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true")); tests that use them must be skipped under the same condition (skip_on_cran()).
  • The test suite does not hit the network: test_model_from_api.R points model_from_api() at local fixtures in tests/testthat/sample_json/. Keep it that way when adding tests for API-backed models.
  • The one test that actually installs a model as a package (test_model_from_api.R, “Can install a package from json”) writes to an explicit temp lib dir and is gated with skip_on_cran(). Follow that pattern for any new installing test; tests that only exercise dispatch (e.g. test_install_default_literature_model.R) mock model_from_api() instead and need neither.

CI

GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/): - R-CMD-check.yaml: R CMD check --as-cran on ubuntu/windows/macOS (R release), run for each push to master and each commit in a PR. Fails only on errors, not warnings/notes. - pkgdown.yaml: Documentation website, run for each commit in a PR - rhub.yaml: Run tests on R-hub, runs only on request

Dependencies

Core: Rcpp (≥1.0.13), BH (Boost headers), data.table, stringr, MASS, randtoolbox, jsonlite, stats, parallel, magrittr. Suggested: httr, testthat (≥3.0.0), knitr, rmarkdown. R ≥ 4.0.0 required.

Keep the dependency footprint small — this is a CRAN package, and new hard dependencies need a good reason.

Repository conventions

  • Documentation is roxygen2 with markdown enabled (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)).
  • Vignettes live in vignettes/; several are excluded from the build via .Rbuildignore because they are slow or need optional packages.
  • Non-standard top-level files must be listed in .Rbuildignore or R CMD check --as-cran reports a NOTE.
  • User-visible changes belong in NEWS.md.
